requirement:
A decorator's attachment span starts at `@` and covers the full decorator
expression, including any arguments.
rationale:
The requirement says a decorator's attachment span starts at `@` and covers the full decorator expression, including any arguments. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[typescript_and_tsx_decorators_belong_to_the_decorated_declaration]` carries a {test} marker for it. The test parses the same source as both `.ts` and `.tsx`. It asserts the exact text of every attachment span, taken as `&source[attachment.span]`, and compares it with an expected list of (selector, text) pairs. The cases are:
- Bare decorators: `@sealed`, `@trace`, `@local`. Each span starts at `@` and ends at the end of the name.
- A decorator with a string argument: `@register("widget")`. The span includes the whole argument list.
- A multi-line decorator with a member-expression callee: `@metrics.time(\n        "render"\n    )`. The span covers the full expression across lines.
- A decorator whose argument contains an arrow function and a nested decorated class: `@published(() => { @local class Local {} })`. The span covers the entire argument, and the nested `@local` gets its own span.
- Decorators on an `export default abstract class`.

The exact-text equality assertions would reject a span that starts after `@`, stops before the arguments, or stops at the first closing paren or brace. The fingerprint and hash edits in the same test give extra evidence that the argument text is part of the attachment. They do not replace the span assertions. I found no unacknowledged gap for this obligation.

text: A decorator's attachment span starts at `@` and covers the full decorator
